input.quote: CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES. COMPANYS' MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO CONTRACTOR FOR ANY REASON ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR.
input.rationale: Section 7(a) caps both parties, and 7(b) mutually excludes indirect/consequential damages, so mutuality is in place. However the cap basis is undefined in duration (fees paid for the relevant Services, which for a short Statement of Work can fall well below six months' fees) and the only exception is a dangling cross-reference to "Paragraph 9" (Independent Contractor), so there are no carve-outs at all for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence or wilful misconduct. That fails the fallback on material terms. We have taken the fallback target: both caps set at fees paid in the 12 months preceding the claim, plus one mutual carve-out sentence. We did not press the preferred USD 1,000,000 floor, data protection/security, fraud, IP-infringement carve-outs or the payment-obligations exclusion.

mappings.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.

proposal.summary: Set both caps at 12 months' fees and add mutual carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have set each party's cap at the fees paid in the 12 months preceding the claim and placed indemnification, confidentiality breaches, gross negligence and wilful misconduct outside the cap, consistent with our fallback position on limitation of liability.
